conditional_corrected_consequence.conditional_elimination: if q does not divide 2^g-1, no solution can exist
conditional_corrected_consequence.gcd_mersenne_sieve: with g=gcd(p-1,q-1), ord_q(2) divides g, hence q divides 2^g-1
conditional_corrected_consequence.gcd_two_subfamily: if gcd(p-1,q-1)=2 and q>3, no solution can exist because the only odd prime divisor of 2^2-1 is 3
conditional_corrected_consequence.imported_hypothesis: accept all preceding ideal-theoretic steps through the conclusion that each prime of Q(zeta_p) above every rational r dividing x*y*(x+y) splits in L/Q(zeta_p)
conditional_corrected_consequence.parity_input: because p and q are odd and x,y are coprime, 2 divides exactly one of x,y,x+y after removing q-adic powers

correct_galois_statement.containment_equivalence: D_r subgroup G' iff n=1 iff r=1 mod q
correct_galois_statement.containment_needed_for_claim: L^(D_r) contains Q(zeta_q) iff D_r is a subgroup of G'
correct_galois_statement.intersection_equivalence: D_r intersect H'={1} iff n divides m
correct_galois_statement.logical_gap: trivial intersection with a direct-product factor does not imply containment in the complementary factor

global_impact.advance: conditional on the preprint's ideal-factorization steps, the corrected decomposition-group argument gives an explicit finite Mersenne-divisor sieve for q at every fixed p and closes every pair failing q | 2^g-1
global_impact.not_enough_for_beal: the surviving repeated-prime pairs and every three-distinct-prime signature remain; the source paper's claimed universal parity contradiction is not valid

nonclaim: The group-theoretic diagnosis is unconditional. The arithmetic order sieve is conditional on the unverified preceding ideal-theoretic lemmas of arXiv:2509.18275. This certificate does not prove the repeated-prime family or Beal.

scope.bases: coprime nonzero integers as in arXiv:2509.18275
scope.q: odd prime q distinct from p

source_claim_audited.claimed_inference: D_r intersect H'={1}, therefore the fixed field L^(D_r) contains K'=Q(zeta_q), hence r splits completely in K'
source_claim_audited.paper: Preda Mihailescu, The strong Fermat-Catalan Equation
